title: 高市早苗首相が初の訪米　米国の待遇や歴代首相との違いは？
extracted_text:
米国の外交上最も格式が高い接遇は国賓で、大統領や国王ら元首級が対象だ。内閣の長である日本の首相もこれに準じた「国賓待遇」にする例がある。通常の公式訪問などと一線を画し、手厚い儀礼でもてなして友好関係を強調する。今回は国賓待遇と銘打っていないものの、夕食会があるなど厚遇といえる。

国賓待遇の場合はホワイトハウスでの歓迎式典に始まり、首脳会談の後に共同記者会見が設けられることが多い。今回は共同記者会見は実施しない見通しだ。宿泊先は一般にホワイトハウスの近くの大統領迎賓館「ブレアハウス」になる。

日本の首相が米国を公式訪問した近年の主な例には15年の安倍晋三氏、24年の岸田文雄氏が挙げられる。いずれも米議会での演説に臨んだ。高市首相は国会答弁で、米側から議会演説の打診を受けたものの日程上の理由で見送ったと説明した。

米国は日本にとって「外交の基軸」とも呼ぶ同盟国だ。日本の歴代首相は就任すると早期訪米の機会を探ってきた。首脳間の関係を早い段階で深め、日米関係の重要性を確認する場として位置づけてきた。

今回の高市首相は25年10月の首相就任からおよそ5カ月で訪米が実現した。訪米は近年の首相の中で際立って早くはないものの、首相の就任直後にトランプ氏を日本に迎えている。半年もたたずに相互訪問が実現するのは珍しい。

石破茂前首相は就任から4カ月だった。日米の懸案として米関税交渉が重要になる状況で、対米投資を1兆ドルにすると打ち出し、関係づくりに力を注いだ。

新型コロナウイルス禍の影響があった岸田氏は1年3カ月、菅義偉氏は7カ月だった。菅氏は当時のバイデン大統領との共同声明で「台湾海峡の平和と安定」という文言を明記した。

今回の訪米は米国とイスラエルによるイラン攻撃後、最初の日米首脳会談になる。首相が日本の姿勢をどう打ち出し、トランプ氏が何を日本に期待するのかが焦点になる。

米国の新たな関税措置や日本の対米投資案件の公表にも関心が集まる。当初はトランプ氏の訪中を前に日米が対中国への考え方を擦り合わせる機会としても想定していた。対中認識を巡るやり取りも重要になる。

高市首相は安倍首相時代の「蜜月関係」を引き継ぎ、トランプ氏との良好なつながりづくりに努めてきた。両首脳は25年10月の日本での初顔合わせから、互いに「ドナルド」「サナエ」と呼びあって親密さを発信した。

首相は「日米同盟の新たな黄金時代をつくりたい」と呼びかけた。米側によるとトランプ氏をノーベル平和賞に推薦する意向も示した。トランプ氏は「彼女とは非常に良い関係を築いている」と強調した。

衆院選の際は選挙戦終盤にトランプ氏が首相と自民党、日本維新の会の連立政権についてSNSで支持を打ち出した。「米大統領として完全かつ全面的に支持する」と投稿した。米大統領が日本の国政選挙で与党への支持を明らかにするのは異例だ。

トランプ氏は衆院選後の2月16日、自民党の圧勝に関し首相が「私の支持を要因に挙げていた」と一方的に主張した。首相は9日、X（旧ツイッター）上で「トランプ大統領の温かいお言葉に心から感謝いたします」と謝意を示していた。

日本の首相はこれまでも同盟国の最高権力者である米大統領との個人的な関係に腐心してきた。安倍氏は16年の大統領選でトランプ氏が当選すると、大統領就任前にニューヨークのトランプタワーを訪れて面会した。

歴代首相がワシントンを訪れる際にも友好関係を演出してきた。高市首相とトランプ氏が今回どのように関係性を象徴する場をつくるかも注目ポイントだ。

translated_text:
The highest diplomatic protocol in US diplomacy is a state visit, reserved for heads of state such as presidents and kings. Japanese prime ministers, as heads of government, have also sometimes received equivalent 'state visit treatment.' This distinguishes it from standard official visits, with elaborate ceremonies emphasizing the friendly relationship. While this visit is not officially labeled a state visit, it includes a dinner and can be considered generous treatment.

In the case of state visits, a welcome ceremony at the White House is typically followed by a joint press conference after summit talks. This time, no joint press conference is planned. Accommodation is normally at Blair House, the presidential guest house near the White House.

Recent Japanese prime ministers who have made official visits to the US include Shinzo Abe in 2015 and Fumio Kishida in 2024. Both delivered speeches to the US Congress. Prime Minister Takai explained that while she received an invitation from the US side to address Congress, she declined due to scheduling reasons.

The US is referred to as Japan's 'diplomatic linchpin' ally. Every Japanese prime minister has sought to visit the US early in their term. They have worked to deepen bilateral relations at an early stage and confirm the importance of the Japan-US alliance.

This visit by Prime Minister Takai occurred about five months after she took office in October 2025. While it is not the fastest among recent prime ministers, she invited Trump to Japan immediately after taking office. Mutual visits within half a year are uncommon.

Former Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba visited Washington four months after taking office. At a time when US tariff negotiations are an important issue between Japan and the US, he announced plans to invest $1 trillion in the US, focusing on building the relationship.

Due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, Prime Minister Kishida took one year and three months, and Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga took seven months. Suga included wording about 'peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait' in a joint statement with President Biden at the time.

This visit to the US marks the first Japan-US summit since the US and Israel carried out attacks on Iran. How the prime minister presents Japan's position and what Trump expects from Japan will be key points of focus.

There is also interest in new US tariff measures and announcements of Japan's US investment plans. Initially, it was expected to be an opportunity for Japan and the US to align their thinking on China ahead of Trump's visit to China. Exchanges regarding views on China will also be important.

Prime Minister Takai has continued the 'honeymoon relationship' from the Abe era and worked to build good rapport with Trump. Since their first meeting in Japan in October 2025, both leaders have addressed each other by their first names, 'Donald' and 'Sanae,' projecting their closeness.

The prime minister has expressed her desire to 'create a new golden era of the Japan-US alliance.' According to the US side, she also indicated intent to nominate Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize. Trump emphasized that he has 'a very good relationship with her.'

During the Lower House election campaign, Trump expressed his support for the prime minister and the LDP-New Japan Party coalition government on social media in the final stages of the campaign. He posted that 'as US president, I give my complete and total support.' It is unusual for a US president to explicitly support Japan's ruling party in a national election.

On February 16 after the Lower House election, Trump unilaterally claimed that the LDP's landslide victory was due to his support. On the 9th, the prime minister had expressed gratitude on X (formerly Twitter), saying, 'I am sincerely grateful for President Trump's warm words.'

Japanese prime ministers have always cared deeply about their personal relationships with US presidents, who are the highest authority in Japan's ally country. When Trump won the 2016 presidential election, Abe visited Trump Tower in New York to meet with him before he took office.

Previous prime ministers have also worked to cultivate friendly relations when visiting Washington. How Prime Minister Takai and Trump will create symbolic moments for their relationship this time will also be a point of interest.
